portName: Port of Palma (Estació Marítima terminals and Dique del Oeste)
seoTitle: Palma cruise port guide: bus 1, terminals, cathedral
seoDescription: Palma cruise port: terminals sit 3.5–6 km from the cathedral. EMT bus 1 costs €2 (2026), the walk is 45+ min, cathedral entry €25 with terraces. Day plan.
quickAnswer: Palma is a docking port, but the cruise berths are 3.5–6 km west of the cathedral. Take EMT bus 1 (€2 cash or card in 2026, about 20 minutes) or your ship's shuttle into town; walking takes 45 minutes or more along the seafront. For a 17:30 all-aboard, be on a bus or taxi back from the centre by 15:45.
intro: Palma's port is large and its cruise berths are a long way from the sights. Ships use the Estació Marítima terminals on the Paraires and Poniente quays, or the outer Dique del Oeste breakwater further west, and which one you get decides how your day starts. Once you reach the cathedral, the Old Town is compact and walkable. Plan around the cathedral's hours: it opens at 10:00 and closes early on Saturdays and all day Sunday to tourist visits.

terminals.name: Estació Marítima terminals 1–4 (Paraires and Poniente quays)
terminals.notes: The inner cruise terminals, linked by covered walkways, off Avinguda de Gabriel Roca. EMT bus 1 stops on Avinguda de Gabriel Roca, opposite Club de Mar, a short walk from the terminal exits. Walkable to the cathedral along the Passeig Marítim in roughly 45–50 minutes.

terminals.name: Dique del Oeste (west breakwater, terminals 5–6)
terminals.notes: Outer berths used by the largest ships, near Porto Pi and the Sant Carles military museum. Not realistically walkable. The nearest EMT bus 1 stop is near the Sant Carles museum, about 12 minutes' walk from the terminal. Most lines run a shuttle from here.

walkability.detail: From terminals 1–4 the route along Avinguda de Gabriel Roca and the Passeig Marítim is flat with a wide seafront promenade, but there is almost no shade and it takes 45–50 minutes to the cathedral. From the Dique del Oeste add another 20–30 minutes. A good compromise is the bus in and a walk back along the seafront if time allows. Inside the Old Town, distances are short but streets climb gently behind the cathedral.

transportSections.cost: €2 single (2026), cash or contactless bank card on board
transportSections.detail: Stops: Avinguda de Gabriel Roca opposite Club de Mar for terminals 1–4; near the Sant Carles military museum for the Dique del Oeste (about 12 minutes' walk). For the cathedral, get off on Avinguda d'Antoni Maura. Drivers give limited change (notes up to €10). Paying by contactless card works for several passengers on one card. Palma city council has approved raising the non-resident single fare to €3, but it had not taken effect as of September 2026; check before travel.

transportSections.cost: Set by each cruise line; some free, some charged
transportSections.detail: Usually drops near the cathedral or Parc de la Mar. Check the price and last return time in your daily programme; on busy days the queue for the last shuttles back can be long.

transportSections.time: 10–15 minutes to the cathedral, longer in traffic
transportSections.detail: Ranks outside the terminals and near the cathedral by Parc de la Mar. Queues form when several ships arrive together. Use only official white taxis.

A new port water-bus service run by Palma Cruises. Lines 2 and 3, aimed at cruise passengers, start on 1 November 2026; line 1 (Poniente quay, La Llotja and the old harbour) starts on 15 January 2027. Stops and timetables were not published at the time of writing.
Stops in front of station 2 at the Poniente quay; from the Dique del Oeste walk about 10 minutes to the Porto Pi stop. Useful for Bellver Castle, which is on a hill and awkward by public transport.

returnTiming.rule: For a 17:30 all-aboard, leave the cathedral area by 15:45 (bus or taxi) and be on board by 16:30. From the Dique del Oeste, leave by 15:30.
returnTiming.detail: Bus 1 takes about 20 minutes but you may wait 10–15 minutes for one, and traffic on the Passeig Marítim slows in the afternoon. Add the walk from the bus stop to your gangway (a few minutes at terminals 1–4, about 12 minutes at the Dique del Oeste) and any security queue at the terminal.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from the rank by Parc de la Mar below the cathedral; it is the fastest way back. Tell the driver the terminal (Estació Marítima or Dique del Oeste) and your ship's name. If you are going to be late, call the port agent number on your daily programme.

excursionAdvice: Palma city does not need a tour; bus 1 or the shuttle plus the cathedral ticket covers it. The ship excursion is worth it for the mountains and north-west coast (Valldemossa, Deià, Sóller and the vintage train), which are 30–60 minutes away on winding roads with limited buses. If you are berthed at the Dique del Oeste and your line charges for the shuttle, compare that cost with a shared taxi.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking 08:00 at the Estació Marítima terminals on a weekday (Monday to Friday).

steps.what: Walk out to Avinguda de Gabriel Roca and take EMT bus 1 towards the centre (€2).
Get off on Avinguda d'Antoni Maura. Walk through Parc de la Mar for the classic view of the cathedral above the lake.
Old Town loop before the cathedral opens: Plaça de Cort, the lanes behind the cathedral and the Banys Àrabs quarter, then Plaça Major.
Palma Cathedral at opening. Allow 75–90 minutes; add the terraces if the timed slot fits (age 9+, not for vertigo or reduced mobility).
Royal Palace of La Almudaina next door (closed Mondays). Allow 45 minutes.
Lunch around La Llotja or Mercat de l'Olivar.
Walk Passeig del Born and the Es Baluard bastion for harbour views, or rest at Can Pere Antoni beach east of the cathedral.
Bus 1 back from Avinguda d'Antoni Maura, or a taxi from Parc de la Mar.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Palma Cathedral (La Seu)
sights.why: Gothic cathedral above the sea, with one of the largest rose windows in Europe and a canopy and side chapel reworked by Gaudí and Miquel Barceló.
sights.cost: €25 general admission including terraces and the Museum of Sacred Art (2026)
sights.tip: Tourist visits Mon–Fri from 10:00, Saturday mornings only, closed Sundays. Terrace visits run Monday–Friday 10:00–16:30 and Saturday 10:00–13:30, a slot every 30 minutes, until November (Majorca Daily Bulletin, March 2026). Cover shoulders and knees; no beachwear.

sights.name: Royal Palace of La Almudaina
sights.why: The former Moorish citadel turned royal residence, beside the cathedral.
sights.tip: Closed Mondays. October–March 10:00–18:00, April–September to 19:00; ticket office closes an hour earlier. It reopened in summer 2026 after renovation.

sights.name: Bellver Castle
sights.why: A round Gothic castle on a pine-covered hill with the widest view over the bay and city.
sights.tip: Closed Mondays. October–March Tue–Sat 10:00–18:00, Sun 10:00–15:00. It is closer to the cruise terminals than to the Old Town, so a taxi from the ship works well.

sights.name: Old Town lanes and Banys Àrabs
sights.why: Courtyard houses, small churches and one of the few surviving buildings from Moorish Palma.
sights.tip: Walk in the morning before the main cruise crowds arrive.

sights.name: Passeig del Born and Plaça Major
sights.why: The main promenade and the arcaded square at the heart of the old city.
sights.tip: Plaça Major is a short walk uphill from the Born; shops and cafés line the route.

sights.name: Es Baluard and the city walls
sights.why: Modern art museum built into a Renaissance bastion; the walls give free views over the harbour.
sights.tip: On the walk between the centre and the port, so useful on the way back.

sights.name: Mercat de l'Olivar
sights.why: The main covered food market, with tapas and seafood counters.
sights.tip: Go before early afternoon; many stalls close after lunch.

beaches.name: Can Pere Antoni
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk east from the cathedral along the seafront path.
beaches.note: The nearest sandy city beach; can be busy and has basic facilities.

beaches.name: Cala Major
beaches.howToGetThere: EMT bus 4 (Joan Miró stop) or a short taxi from the terminals.
beaches.note: Small sandy bay west of the port, close to the cruise berths, so a lower-risk choice for a swim.

beaches.name: Ses Illetes
beaches.note: Clear water and small coves; sun loungers fill early in summer.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the cathedral is a short walk from the ship.
commonMistakes.fix: It is 3.5–6 km depending on your berth. Take bus 1 or the shuttle in.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arriving at the cathedral before 10:00 or on a Sunday.
commonMistakes.fix: Tourist visits start at 10:00 and are not offered on Sundays; use early morning for the Old Town.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up in beachwear or vest tops for the cathedral.
commonMistakes.fix: Cover shoulders and knees; carry a light layer.

commonMistakes.mistake: Waiting for the last shuttle back.
commonMistakes.fix: Shuttle and taxi queues peak an hour before sailing. Head back by 15:45 for a 17:30 all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Handing the bus driver a €20 or €50 note.
commonMistakes.fix: Drivers give limited change. Use a contactless card or carry small notes and coins.

safety: Palma is generally safe for visitors. Pickpocketing is the main risk, particularly around the cathedral, Passeig del Born, Plaça Major and on crowded buses. Keep phones off café tables. In summer the seafront walk to and from the port is long, hot and unshaded, so heat is the more likely problem; carry water.
scams: Pickpockets working crowds around the cathedral and Plaça Major, sometimes using distraction (a map, a petition or a spilt drink): keep bags zipped and in front.
Rosemary or flower sellers near the cathedral who press a sprig into your hand and then demand money: decline and keep walking.
Unofficial 'taxi' offers near the terminals: use the official taxi rank and metered white taxis only.
accessibility: The seafront route from the terminals to the centre is flat with wide pavements, and EMT buses are low-floor with ramps. The approach to the cathedral from Parc de la Mar involves steps; a gentler route runs up via Avinguda d'Antoni Maura and the Almudaina side. The Old Town has narrow, sometimes uneven streets with gentle climbs. The cathedral terraces are not open to people with reduced mobility. Palma is a docking port, so there are no tender transfers.
rainyDay: Spend longer in the cathedral and the Museum of Sacred Art included with the ticket, then the Almudaina palace next door. Es Baluard museum and the Fundació Miró Mallorca (near Cala Major, close to the port) are good indoor options. Mercat de l'Olivar is covered and works for lunch.
crowdTips: Palma often has three to five ships in one day in high season. The cathedral queue builds from 10:00 to midday; buy a timed ticket online and go at opening or after 14:00 on weekdays. Saturday visits finish early, so Saturday calls are especially busy. The terraces have a limited number of places per slot. Buses on line 1 fill up with cruise passengers in the first hour after docking; walking a few minutes to an earlier stop does not help, so be patient or take a taxi with others.

faqs.q: Is Palma walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Partly. From terminals 1–4 it is about 3.5 km, or 45–50 minutes, along the flat seafront to the cathedral. From the Dique del Oeste it is around 6 km and not practical. Most people take bus 1 in and some walk back.

faqs.q: How do I get from Palma cruise port to the cathedral?
faqs.a: Take EMT bus 1 (€2 in 2026, cash or contactless) and get off on Avinguda d'Antoni Maura, below the cathedral. The ride is about 20 minutes. Alternatives are the ship's shuttle or a taxi.

faqs.q: Is Palma de Mallorca a tender port?
faqs.a: No. All cruise ships berth alongside, either at the Estació Marítima terminals or on the Dique del Oeste.
General admission is €25 in 2026, including the terraces and the Museum of Sacred Art. Under-9s cannot go on the terraces.

faqs.q: What can I do in Palma in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The cathedral, the Almudaina palace, the Old Town, Passeig del Born and lunch at Mercat de l'Olivar fill a day comfortably. With extra time, add Bellver Castle or a swim at Cala Major.

faqs.q: Are there beaches near Palma cruise port?
faqs.a: Cala Major and Ses Illetes are west of the port, 10–30 minutes by bus 4 or taxi. Can Pere Antoni is the nearest city beach to the cathedral.

faqs.q: Is Palma safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. The main risk is pickpocketing in crowds around the cathedral and Old Town. Keep valuables zipped away.

faqs.q: Which cruise terminal will my ship use in Palma?
faqs.a: The port assigns berths, and they can change shortly before arrival. Larger ships often use the Dique del Oeste. Check your daily programme or the ship's port talk.
